summaryBox.takeaway: Schleiden & Schwann proposed cell theory; Rudolf Virchow modified it with 'Omnis cellula-e-cellula' (cells arise from pre-existing cells).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
HISTORICAL CELL THEORY MILESTONES
                                          │
  Robert Hooke (1665)    ──► Discovered dead cork cells ("cellulae")
  A. v. Leeuwenhoek (1674)──► First observed living cells ("animalcules" - bacteria, protozoa)
  Schleiden & Schwann    ──► Formulated Classical Cell Theory (1838 - Plants / 1839 - Animals)
  Rudolf Virchow (1855)  ──► Added *Omnis cellula-e-cellula* (All cells arise from pre-existing cells)
conceptBreakdown.content:
The cell is the fundamental, structural, functional, and physiological unit of all living organisms.

### Modern Cell Theory Postulates
1. **Composition**: All living organisms are composed of one or more cells and their secretory/metabolic products.
2. **Biogenesis**: All cells arise from pre-existing cells via mitotic or meiotic cell division (*Omnis cellula-e-cellula*, Rudolf Virchow, 1855).
3. **Genetic Continuity**: Cells pass hereditary information (DNA) to daughter cells during division.
4. **Metabolic Unity**: All energy flow and biochemical metabolic pathways occur within cells.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.1 Structural Limits on Cell Dimensions
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.1 Structural Limits on Cell Dimensions
conceptBreakdown.content:
Cellular dimensions are physically constrained by two critical parameters:

### 1. Surface Area-to-Volume Constraint ($SA/V$)
As a spherical or cuboidal cell expands in radius ($r$), its surface area increases as $r^2$, while its internal metabolic volume increases as $r^3$. Beyond a critical threshold, the membrane surface area becomes inadequate to exchange nutrients, gases, and wastes for the massive cytoplasmic volume.

### 2. Nucleo-Cytoplasmic Ratio (Karyoplasmic Index - KI)
$$\Large \mathbf{\text{Karyoplasmic Index } (KI) = \frac{V_n}{V_c - V_n}}$$
where $V_n$ is nuclear volume and $V_c$ is total cell volume. A high $KI$ indicates a nucleus capable of commanding its cytoplasm; when cytoplasmic volume outgrows nuclear control capacity, cell division is triggered.

### Size Spectrum Across Life
• **Smallest free-living cells**: *Mycoplasma gallisepticum* / PPLO ($\approx 0.1\text{--}0.3\ \mu\text{m}$).
• **Typical Eubacteria**: $1\text{--}2\ \mu\text{m}$ in length.
• **Typical Eukaryotic cells**: $10\text{--}20\ \mu\text{m}$.
• **Largest isolated single cell**: Ostrich egg (*Struthio camelus* — $170\text{ mm} \times 130\text{ mm}$).
• **Longest human cells**: Motor Neurons ($>1\text{ meter}$).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.2 Prokaryotic vs. Eukaryotic Structural Matrix
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.2 Prokaryotic vs. Eukaryotic Structural Matrix
conceptBreakdown.content:
| Anatomical Parameter | Prokaryotic Cell Architecture | Eukaryotic Cell Architecture |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nuclear Envelope** | **Absent**; genetic material exists as a naked **Nucleoid** | **Present**; enclosed by a double-membrane envelope with Nuclear Pore Complexes |
| **Membrane-Bound Organelles** | **Absent** (no ER, Golgi, Mitochondria, Plastids, Lysosomes) | **Present** (highly compartmentalized cytoplasm) |
| **Ribosome Profile** | **70S** (30S subunit + 50S subunit) in cytoplasm | **80S** (40S subunit + 60S subunit) in cytoplasm; 70S inside organelles |
| **Genetic Material** | Single, circular, double-stranded DNA; **Lacks Histone proteins** | Multiple linear double-stranded DNA molecules; **Bound to Histones** |
| **Cell Wall Biochemistry** | Composed of **Peptidoglycan** (Bacteria) or Pseudopeptidoglycan (Archaea) | Composed of **Cellulose** (Plants/Algae) or **Chitin** (Fungi); absent in animals |
| **Cytoskeleton** | Primitive homologues (FtsZ, MreB, ParM) | Highly organized network of **Microtubules**, **Microfilaments**, and **Intermediate Filaments** |
| **Flagellar Architecture** | Single-strand helical **Flagellin** protein; rotary motion driven by basal motor | Complex **$9+2$ Axoneme** arrangement of Tubulin doublets; sliding dynein motion |
| **Cell Division** | Binary Fission / Amitosis (Lacks mitotic spindle apparatus) | **Mitosis** and **Meiosis** involving a microtubular spindle apparatus |
